source_title: Dragon Ball Z: 6 Ways the Cell Saga Changed the Franchise Forever
source_excerpt:
Over the years, the Dragon Ball franchise has introduced some of the greatest and most iconic story arcs in anime history. From the rampage of the Saiyans on Earth to the tyranny of Frieza on Namek, these arcs have become staples in the anime industry and have shaped the series into the massive and incredible media force that it has become in today's world.
When asking fans about the best arc in the entire franchise, answers are mixed, but the Cell Saga is a common response. Not only was this arc one of the best in terms of what it showed and how it served the characters, but it also changed the trajectory of the franchise going forward .
6 It Showed That Refinement Is Better Than Raw Strength
One of the most recognizable aspects of Dragon Ball is the many transformations that have been introduced. From the series' early days, characters have been shown to get stronger through the unlocking of powerful new forms, and while that remains true for the Cell Saga , this story arc proved that raw strength isn't always the correct way to grow in overall power.
The best example of this came once Trunks unveiled his Super Saiyan Grade 3 state, which was perhaps the most physically powerful form in the story at that point. However, it was very slow and used up too much energy, and on the flip side, Goku and Gohan chose to master and refine Super Saiyan 1 to be much more efficient instead of relying on pure physical power at the cost of speed. This principle can be seen in the modern day with forms like Ultra Instinct and Ultra Ego.
5 It Introduced One of the Most Important Storylines
black clover anime swordsmen who can defeat asta
The Cell Saga essentially deals with the aftermath of the Android Saga, which was the entire reason why Future Trunks traveled back in time to prevent it in the first place. Inadvertently, this led to the birth of Cell, who was a far greater and more destructive threat than any of the other Androids could possibly have been.
Ultimately, the villain was defeated, and Trunks was made all the more powerful because of it, allowing him to go back to his original timeline to finally bring peace. Due to the events of the Cell Saga, the future timeline became a staple within the franchise going forward and would play an incredibly significant role in Super with the beloved Goku Black Arc.
4 It Showed the Consequences of Vegeta's Pride
Vegeta reaction to Trunks death Perfect Cell
For many, Vegeta's redemption arc goes down as the greatest ever seen in the anime industry, and for good reason too, since he went from a planet-destroying supervillain to one of the universe's greatest protectors . As such, it can't be denied that the Cell Saga played one of the greatest roles in delivering this redemption arc, due to how Vegeta learned from it.
Pride has always been Vegeta's defining personality trait, but the Cell Saga was instrumental in examining how it can be the architect of one's downfall. Due to Vegeta's own hubris and overconfidence in his strength after he unlocked new forms, he allowed the threats that he went up against to eventually become far more dangerous, which ended up bringing about far more destruction and terror than they would have otherwise. By the end, Vegeta realizes that pride has a cost, changing him fundamentally.
3 It Showed the Consequences of the Heroes' Actions
Perfect Cell puts a finger to his head. Image via Toei Animation.
The events of the Cell Saga were some of the most dangerous in the franchise, with the entire Earth essentially being forced to be the hostage of a supremely powerful and evil bio-android. Unlike many of the story arcs of Dragon Ball , some of the worst things in the Cell Saga were brought about directly due to the choices made by the heroes.
For example, the Androids were formed in the first place due to Dr. Gero wanting revenge on what Goku had done to the Red Ribbon Army, and Cell himself traveled to this timeline as a result of Trunks' time travel shenanigans. On top of this, he only reached his Perfect form due to Vegeta's overconfidence in his own abilities, and Goku's faith in Gohan almost backfired when the young Saiyan hesitated to finish off the villain. All of these were consequences of what the heroes had done in the past.
2 It Showed That Goku Didn’t Always Have to Be the Hero
When the franchise began, Goku had always been the central figure whose importance to the overall story was far greater than that of everyone else. Subsequently, each arc since then saw Goku be the one to defeat the ultimate villain, which is typically the formula for most fictional stories of a similar nature used for their protagonists.
However, the Cell Saga was different. It placed a ton of focus on the fact that others needed to be around after Goku, and the main hero himself agreed that others needed to build their strength up just as much without needing to rely on him all the time. This was perfectly mirrored at the end, with Gohan unlocking a new state, becoming the strongest of them all, and taking Goku's throne as Earth's greatest protector.
1 The Cell Saga Changed Power Scaling Forever
During the closing moments of the Namek Saga, fans were introduced to the new standard going forward, which was the legendary Super Saiyan form. For much of the subsequent Android and Cell Sagas, the mastery of Super Saiyan became a top priority for the heroes, but this all changed with the end of the arc, when Gohan shattered all limits to unlock Super Saiyan 2. From here, the ceiling of power was changed forever, and the heights that the heroes could reach following this time were essentially limitless.
In the following Buu Saga and Dragon Ball Super series, the Saiyans' transformations got a serious boost due to a practice that is still followed in the franchise today, even with the incredible Divine Forms that are now the norm, and this entire trend was started in the first place by the Cell Saga.
